description: The configuration surface of the kafka chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

cruiseControl.description: Cruise Control — partition rebalancing and broker-load reporting.

enabled.description: Whether Cruise Control runs. On by default: docs/plan/12 puts it in the chart rather than in a follow-up, because rebalancing a Kafka cluster by hand is the operational cost that makes this the most demanding service in the catalogue.

external.description: Exposure outside the cluster, via a load balancer and a firewall allow-list.

allowedCidrs.description: Source ranges permitted to reach the external listener. Required in substance rather than in schema: an empty list with external exposure on renders a load balancer that accepts nothing, which is the safe reading of an unfinished configuration.

enabled.description: Whether the cluster is reachable from outside the Kubernetes cluster. Off by default — docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions makes external exposure never the default, because a managed broker on a public IP with a weak password is the most common cloud breach there is.

imageName.description: Override the operator's default Kafka image. Empty means the operator chooses, which is what keeps minor upgrades automatic.
imageName.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: A pinned image defeats automatic minor upgrades, so it is a platform escape hatch rather than a tenant setting.

listener.description: The in-cluster listener every client reaches.

tls.description: Whether the in-cluster listener requires TLS. On by default; turning it off is a plaintext broker on the pod network.

enabled.description: Whether the operator runs a Kafka Exporter alongside the cluster, exposing consumer-lag and topic metrics to the platform's metrics stack.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

nodes.description: Number of Kafka nodes, each acting as both a KRaft controller and a broker. Use an odd number: a quorum of two tolerates no failures, and one is a single point of failure offered for development only.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

retention.description: How long the cluster keeps messages by default. docs/plan/12 calls retention sizing an ongoing operational concern rather than a one-time setting.

hours.description: Default retention in hours. A week by default.

size.description: Default retention by partition size, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means retention is by time alone.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per node, either by preset or explicitly.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

class.description: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

deleteClaim.description: Whether deleting the resource also deletes the log volumes. Off by default, so a mistaken delete leaves the data recoverable by hand.

size.description: Log volume size per node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

topics.description: Defaults applied to topics the cluster creates automatically. A topic created explicitly overrides them.

minInSyncReplicas.description: How many replicas must acknowledge a write before it is committed. Must be below the replication factor, or the cluster cannot tolerate one broker restart.

partitions.description: Default partition count for a new topic.

replicationFactor.description: Default replication factor for a new topic. Must not exceed the node count, or every produce to a new topic fails.

version.description: Apache Kafka version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window; a major upgrade is an explicit update to this field.
